source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Counting linear extensions is fixed-parameter intractable under cover-graph treewidth unless W[1]=FPT; this is an order-counting obstruction, not a reduction to weighted random isolation.
The article gives an O-tilde(n^(t+3)) cover-treewidth algorithm for counting linear extensions and handles joins by multivariate-polynomial multiplication.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Add a worked width-two or width-three conflict-graph instance that explicitly computes a tagged polynomial, its Q matrix, and the resulting finite-library SDP certificate; this would make the separator state target auditable before the general dichotomy is solved.

State a parameter-preserving reduction target for the negative branch more narrowly—source problem, encoding of its order constraint into a marked coefficient, and the intended bound on conflict-treewidth—so hardness is falsifiable rather than merely aspirational.

Add a precise proposition locating the restricted WRI/RDIM oracle relative to the maximal-independent-set formulation of KandirosHarshawSavje2026, including the map between the two conflict graphs and the exact restriction that prevents subsumption.
Clarify that the identity term in H^{-1}=I+gamma L_C bounds componentwise level shifts while the Laplacian term penalizes edge variation; give a radius scaling for bounded endpoints.

recommended_next_step: Advance this field-grade proposal to Stage 0, prioritizing either a separator-message closure invariant or a parameter-preserving marked-coefficient hardness reduction.
